stages.name: Exploitation of Public-Facing Services
observables: Microsoft Exchange Server stack-based buffer overflow (CVE-2026-70571)
Windows DHCP Server use-after-free (CVE-2026-96934, CVE-2026-88117, CVE-2026-88119, CVE-2026-88120)
Network Device Enrollment Service (NDES) weak authentication (CVE-2026-69802)

stages.name: Client-Side RCE and Command Injection
observables: Microsoft Excel remote code execution (CVE-2026-100211, CVE-2026-97739)
Microsoft Outlook remote code execution (CVE-2026-70242, CVE-2026-97749)
Windows Media Foundation heap buffer overflow (CVE-2026-96952)

stages.name: Kernel and VBS Enclave Escalation
observables: Windows Virtualization-Based Security (VBS) Enclave race condition (CVE-2026-102211)

stages.name: Lateral Movement via AD and RDS
observables: Windows Active Directory Domain Services incorrect authorization (CVE-2026-70229)
AD FS spoofing via improper certificate validation (CVE-2026-96222)

scenario.summary: The October 2026 Microsoft security update addresses 141 vulnerabilities, including a Windows Shell command injection 0-day exploited in the wild and critical RCEs in Active Directory, Exchange, and Office. The campaign involves potential initial access via vulnerable public-facing services or phishing, followed by kernel-level privilege escalation and lateral movement through Remote Desktop and Active Directory flaws.

hunt.name: October 2026 Patch Tuesday Exposure Hunt
hunt.description: This hunt identifies exposure to the critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities disclosed in the October 2026 Microsoft Patch Tuesday, including the Windows Shell 0-day (CVE-2026-96951). It follows the exposure flow: first identifying unpatched hosts via vulnerability findings joined with device inventory, then examining rare process activity on those hosts, and finally monitoring for high-confidence behavioral indicators like web servers or productivity applications spawning command shells.

config.content: SELECT d.hostname, v.cve_uid, v.severity, v.status, v.first_seen FROM hb_vulnerability_finding v JOIN hb_devices d ON v.device_uid = d.device_uid WHERE instr(',' || '{{critical_cves}}' || ',', ',' || v.cve_uid || ',') > 0 AND v.status != 'suppressed' ORDER BY v.severity_id DESC
config.description: Locate systems where vulnerability scanners have identified missing patches for the critical October 2026 CVEs, joining with device inventory for direct hostname mapping.
config.expected_signal: Rows identify specific assets by hostname that remain unpatched. Silence means no hosts are reporting these specific vulnerabilities.

primitive_config.label: Identify unpatched vulnerable hosts
primitive_config.content: SELECT d.hostname, v.cve_uid, v.severity, v.status, v.first_seen FROM hb_vulnerability_finding v JOIN hb_devices d ON v.device_uid = d.device_uid WHERE instr(',' || '{{critical_cves}}' || ',', ',' || v.cve_uid || ',') > 0 AND v.status != 'suppressed' ORDER BY v.severity_id DESC
primitive_config.expected: Rows identify specific assets by hostname that remain unpatched. Silence means no hosts are reporting these specific vulnerabilities.

config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_path) AS path, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= '2026-10-13' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY path HAVING host_count <= 3 ORDER BY host_count ASC
config.description: Identify unusual binaries on vulnerable systems to detect first-stage payloads.
config.expected_signal: A binary or script seen on only 1-3 hosts since the patch disclosure. Silence suggests no unique execution occurred on the scoped hosts.

primitive_config.label: Stack-count rare processes

nodes.label: Anomalous shell spawning from vulnerable apps

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, parent_process_name, process_name, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE LOWER(parent_process_name) IN ('c:\windows\system32\inetsrv\w3wp.exe', 'c:\program files\microsoft office\root\office16\excel.exe', 'c:\program files\microsoft office\root\office16\winword.exe', 'c:\program files\microsoft office\root\office16\outlook.exe') AND LOWER(process_name) IN ('c:\windows\system32\cmd.exe', 'c:\windows\system32\windowspowershell\v1.0\powershell.exe', 'c:\windows\system32\mshta.exe') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= '2026-10-13' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Detect successful exploitation of Exchange or Office by monitoring for shells spawned from their respective processes, focused on activity since the patch disclosure.
config.expected_signal: A shell or script interpreter spawned by a web server or productivity application. This indicates remote code execution.

config.success_criteria: A list of hosts classified as 'Exploited', 'Exposed and Anomalous', or 'Exposed but Clean'.
